source: Written by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) from the county counts (AP via The New York Times), the 2024 baseline and Census ACS 2023 context.

47001.t:
In the U.S. Senate race between Hagerty and Bradshaw, Anderson County stayed Republican but by far less than in 2024. Hagerty won 13,663 votes to 9,521, an 18-point margin, after Trump carried the county by 36 points. That 18-point move toward the Democrats ranks seventh of Tennessee's 95 counties, all of which moved left. It runs ahead of the typical Tennessee county (14 points) and roughly matches the statewide shift of 18. It also outpaced similar counties such as Washington (16), Wilson (17) and Lauderdale (14).

Turnout fell sharply: 23,688 votes, about 65% of the 2024 total. The count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

Every one of Tennessee's 95 counties moved left. Lake's shift ranks 26th, a little larger than the typical county's 14 points but short of the state's overall 18-point move. Similar counties moved by comparable amounts: Trousdale 16 points, Humphreys 15 and Houston 13.
